Months to break even (the costs divided by the monthly saving): {col:refi.breakeven}. Check: {col:refi.flag}. Check with your own adviser before you sign.

Open Start and type your company name and your own limits in the yellow cells: the lowest DSCR, the highest loan share a lender allows, the loan-to-value you want to stay under and the days to warn before a balloon date.

Write every loan on Loans with the lender, the type, the amount, the rate, the term, the start date and the balloon date. The monthly payment, the balance today, the share paid down and the interest of the last 12 months fill in.
Record each monthly payment on Loan payments with the interest, the principal and the date paid. Late payments show the days late.
Read Loan to value and DSCR by property to see the loan balance against the value and the income against the loan payments, the room to borrow and the cushion.
List every refinance offer on Refinance options. The saving a month and the months to break even show which offers pay back, and the Cash-out refinance calculator shows the cash released.
Write a plan for each balloon loan on Balloon plan. The balance due and the days left fill in, and the date turns red inside your warning days.
Keep payoff quotes, covenant checks, rate changes and interest-only periods on their own pages, and the lender documents with their due dates.
Use Credit line draws for the line of credit and Private lender terms to see the true yearly rate of a private loan.
Use the 14 calculators: amortisation, interest-only, balance, refinance break-even, cash-out, loan-to-value, DSCR test, balloon planner, rates, extra payment, private cost and a grid.
Read the Loans and Refinance Dashboard and Charts every month: balance by lender and type, interest against principal, loan-to-value, DSCR, balloon dates, refinance saving and late payments.
Figures for tax, interest and sales are estimates: check with your own adviser before you act on them.
Every rehab budget, draw and flip profit in one workbook
Rehab budgets, contractor draws and flip profit for real estate investors
the budget, the cost to date and the overrun of every work category and every project, with a flag when a line runs over
Contractor draw release calculator with retainage
contract, percent complete and retainage become the draw to release now, and every draw shows its inspection check
Flip profit forecast with the actual cost
each project turns its real cost, holding cost and value after the work into a forecast profit and a return
three bids with their scope gaps and days become the true cost of each and the best value
the change amount, the budget and the value become the new total and the effect on the profit
loan interest, tax, insurance and utilities for each month a property sits in work, with the cost of a delay
days late and the holding cost a day become the cost of the delay for each week
planned date, done date and days late for every milestone, with overdue ones flagged
every small job with the date found, the date fixed and the days open, so nothing is forgotten before the sale
the value after the work, the price and the profit you want become the most you can spend on the rehab
Share of each draw held back until the work is finished
Contingency as a share of the rehab budget
Overrun above this share of the budget is flagged
Agent and closing costs when you sell
The 70% rule: highest offer as a share of the ARV
Profit you want from a flip
Rehab lines: budget and actual cost by category
One row for each work category of a project with the budget, the actual cost, the contractor and the dates; the variance and a budget flag fill in, so an overrun shows at once.
Contractor draws: request, inspection and payment
One row for each draw (a payment released to a contractor as work is finished) with the percent complete; the retainage held back, the days to pay and an inspection check fill in.
The 16 properties with the price, the rehab budget and the value now; the total cost and the rehab share of it fill in.
Projects: budget, cost to date and forecast profit
One row for each property with the budget, the value after the work (ARV) and the planned end; spent, forecast cost, overrun, schedule, holding cost and the forecast profit fill in.
One row for each bid with the price, the days to finish and the cost of anything left out (scope gap); the true bid, the saving against the budget and the contractor phone fill in.
Change orders: extra work and its cost
One row for each change to the scope with the reason and the amount; the share of the line budget, the approved amount and the contractor phone fill in.
Milestones: planned date against done date
One row for each milestone of a project with the planned date and the date it was done; the days late and a timing check fill in, so a slip shows early.
Permits: applied, approved and the fee
One row for each permit with the date applied, the date approved and the fee; the days waiting and a flag for what is still pending fill in. Check your own local rules for what each job needs.
One row for each material order with the date promised and the date delivered; the days late and a delivery check fill in, so a late delivery stops the work early.
Punch list: small jobs to finish before handover
One row for each small job found on a walk-through with the date found and the date fixed; the days open and a flag fill in.
Contractors by trade with jobs and spend
One row for each trade with the contractor who does it and a rating; the jobs, the spend and the overrun on finished work fill in from Rehab lines.
Holding costs while a property is being worked on
One row for each property and month with the loan interest, the tax, the insurance and the utilities; the total for the month fills in.
Contingency used: surprises paid from the reserve
One row for each surprise paid from the contingency (the reserve inside a budget); the share of the project contingency fills in.
Flip sale plan: list price options and the profit of each
Six list price options for each flip with the expected sale price; the selling costs, the net sale, the total cost and the profit fill in, with a check against the profit you want.
Scope templates: typical cost by category
One row for each work category with the typical cost per bedroom and the typical days, worked out from your past jobs; the number of jobs of that category fills in.
Draw schedule: planned draws against paid draws
One row for each planned draw with the percent of the work and the planned date; the amount paid, the paid date and a timing check fill in from Draws.
Draw inspections: what the inspector found
One row for each draw inspection with the result and the percent complete found on site; the percent claimed, the gap and the draw amount fill in from Draws.
The loans with the lender, the type, the amount and the rate; the interest each month fills in. Draws on a flip loan follow its schedule.
Budget used on projects in progress
Average saving of the bids chosen
Average days late of late milestones
Spent and draws paid by month
Renovation scope sheet for one project
Spent as a share of the budget
Profit as a share of the total cost
Type the rooms, the floor area, the kitchen, the bathrooms and the trades with unit costs; see the cost of each category, the contingency (a reserve inside the budget) and the total budget.
Floor area to replace in square metres
Budget against actual with a forecast
Type the budget, what you have spent and the percent complete; see the forecast final cost, the overrun and the money left to finish the work.
Cost to finish at this pace
Contractor draw to release with retainage
Type the contract, the percent complete, the retainage (a share of each draw held back until the work is finished) and what you paid so far; see the draw to release now.
Type the contract, the retainage share and the work drawn so far; see the retainage held now, the amount held at the end and what the contractor has been paid.
Paid to the contractor so far
Retainage at the end of the contract
Bid comparison with scope gaps and delay
Type three bids with the cost of what each leaves out (the scope gap) and the days each needs; see the true cost of each, the best value and the gap to the next bid.
Gap to the next best bid
Change order impact on the flip profit
Type the change amount, the budget, the total cost, the value after the work (ARV) and the value the change adds; see the new rehab total and the effect on the profit.
Change as a share of the budget
Flip profit forecast with holding costs
Type the price, the closing costs, the rehab cost, the value after the work (ARV), the months and the holding cost; see the profit, the return on the cost and the highest offer by the 70% rule.
Share of the ARV for the 70% rule
Holding cost per month and the cost of a delay
Type the loan, its rate, the yearly tax and insurance and the monthly utilities; see the cost of holding the property each month and what a delay costs.
Type the days the work is late, the holding cost each month and any extra site cost a day; see what the delay costs in total and for each week.
Extra site cost of the delay
Cost of each week of delay
Maximum rehab spend (the 70% rule and your profit)
Type the value after the work (ARV), the price and the profit you want; see the most you can spend on the rehab by the 70% rule (offer at most 70% of the ARV minus the rehab) and by your profit.
Holding cost for the whole job
Highest price for the planned rehab
Contingency check against the work left
Type the budget, the contingency share, what is used and the share of the work left; see the reserve left and whether it covers the surprises you can expect.
Expected overrun on the work left
Reserve after the expected extra cost
Cost per square metre and per bedroom against past jobs
Type the rehab cost, the area and the bedrooms with the figures of your past jobs; see the cost per square metre and per bedroom and how far you are from the past jobs.
Past jobs: cost per square metre
Against past jobs per square metre
Cost above past jobs for this area
Value added for each unit spent on the work
Type the cost of one piece of work and the value it adds; see the value for each unit spent, the net gain and the return on the work after selling costs.
Value added for each unit spent
Value needed to break even after selling costs
What-if grid: overrun against sale price
Type the flip; each row of the grid shows the profit and the return when the rehab runs over by a share and the sale price moves by a share.
